tier_PROPOSED: safe now (facts, not text) — R1's own posture for peer-reviewed primaries — via the 2009 ACM paper; the website is pointer-only
permits_us: paraphrase — the model's content (three elements must converge: motivation, ability, prompt; B=MAP) as facts in Apollo's words, cited by DOI; names-only for anything from behaviormodel.org; no verbatim paper text
why_our_words: Same posture as Fitts or Cowan in R1's register: the finding is citable, the prose is the publisher's. The website adds nothing a node needs that the paper does not, and it carries no licence, so it should be the pointer and the DOI the source. This is a STUDIED-grade family in s237-D1 terms and the licence risk of holding it as facts is the same as for every other primary already in 'safe now'.
cheap_route_to_lift: Not needed for facts-only. For website text: bj@bjfogg.com is on the page. Price: one email.
unproven: The text of ACM's copyright policy (#Background) — the URL the Crossref licence field names — FAILED in this fetcher. What ACM permits third parties without a fee (e.g. short quotation) is therefore not quoted here. Price: one browser-client fetch (~2K).
Whether behaviormodel.org's rendered page carries a footer notice this fetcher dropped (the response had no header block, unlike every other page). Price: one browser-client fetch (~1K).
Whether 'Fogg Behavior Model' or 'Fogg Behavior Design' is a registered mark — not checked; a node NAME that uses the term is a name, not a trade use, but this lane does not rule on it.

pitfalls.what: The website's short 'simplest explanation' sentence is quotable and memorable; a generator will want to emit it verbatim. It has no licence behind it. Hold the family at facts-in-our-words.
R1 tensions 9 and 19 pair persuasion nodes with DSA Art. 25; Fogg is a persuasion model. The legal fence matters more than the licence here — a Fogg node without its DSA pair is the bigger liability.
